subject: Azure private offer renewal & invoice-bucket / usage handoff
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.t@somnihealth.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal coordination: Azure private offer + invoice cadence

Hi Mina,

We’re coming up on our renewal window for the Azure private offer and I wanted to get a single-threaded plan for paperwork and billing. High level: Somni Health would like to
- extend the term to 24 months (rolling from current expiry on 2027-08-15)
- increase committed capacity ~30% (estimate ~1.3x current average monthly usage)
- request quarterly invoicing (invoice buckets) rather than a single upfront yearly bill
- confirm SLA target of 99.9% for the uplifted tier (this is important for compliance)

Can you confirm the process and timing for a private-offer amendment? Procurement would like a PO-ready PDF that they can sign and return (net-45 preferred). Also please loop in whoever handles marketplace private offer submission so we can align on acceptance timing — we’d like the private offer live within 3 business days after signature if possible.

I’ve cc’d procurement at procurement@somnihealth.com for visibility.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Director of IT Procurement, Somni Health
--
Somni Health | alicia.t@somnihealth.com
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: Azure private offer + invoice cadence

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear summary. We can do the 24‑month term + 30% uplift and support quarterly invoicing; a couple of quick clarifying items so we scope the PO correctly:

1) Usage baseline: can you share the last 3 months' committed vs actual usage (tokens/embeddings) so Marcus can map capacity tiers and recommend the right SKU split?
2) Billing cadence: quarterly invoices are fine. Confirm net-45 and whether each invoice needs a separate PO number or a single master PO with invoice line references.
3) SLA: we can propose a 99.9% SLA exception tied to the committed uplift for the term; legal will need an explicit clause. Kim, can you review SLA language/exception?

Next steps: I’ll draft a PO template and send a PO-ready PDF for procurement to sign. Attaching a Somni_Azure_PO_Template.xlsx (internal template) — will convert to a final PDF once we have the usage baseline and procurement PO number. We’ll also open a HubSpot deal (D-8841) and prepare the private offer in AWS marketplace after signature.

Target timeline:
- Today / tomorrow: confirm baseline and procurement details
- +1 business day: send draft PO for procurement review
- Once signed: publish private offer within 3 business days (contingent on marketplace processing)

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Mina — thanks. Attached is our draft PO (Somni_PO_2027_draft.pdf). Procurement confirms:
- quarterly invoices (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) with net-45 terms
- they will provide separate invoice reference numbers per invoice (preferred)
- expected average monthly usage after uplift ~ 1.3x current (we included a simple usage table in the PDF)

Procurement contact for routing signed docs: procurement@somnihealth.com (Sarah Lee, Sr Manager).

If you can return a PO-ready PDF with the legal SLA clause included, procurement will review and push it to our finance team.

On the SLA: our compliance team needs the 99.9% commitment written into the amendment; if you can propose monitoring and credit terms that will help speed approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alicia

Looping in operations and billing to confirm internal constraints. Quick notes from legal ops:
- I’ve redlined the draft PO with SLA language that ties a 99.9% uptime credit (pro-rated daily, capped at 5% of quarterly invoice) to the committed uplift. See attached PO_redlines_Somni_v2.pdf.
- Marketplace private offer: we can publish an updated private offer after signature, but the marketplace typically takes 24–72 hours to process — not guaranteed. We should set expectation to "within 3 business days" post-signature but avoid committing to sub-24 hour turnaround.
- Marcus: confirm whether the current SKU/instance mix supports the 30% uplift without an immediate dedicated capacity allocation. If not, propose a short ramp credit (30 days) or partial dedicated reservation.

Ben, can you draft the DocuSign envelope and include the PO+redlines as attachments? Include procurement@somnihealth.com as signing recipient.

Kim
